Instantaneous evapotranspiration from the latent heat flux

Source: R/metric-et.R
ef_et_inst.Rd

Converts the instantaneous latent heat flux \(LE\) into the instantaneous evapotranspiration rate \(ET_{inst}\), expressed as a depth of water per hour. The result is a rate evaluated at the satellite overpass time, not a depth accumulated over an hour.

Usage

ef_et_inst(le, lambda)

Arguments

le

Numeric. Instantaneous latent heat flux \(LE\) [W m-2], for example from ef_latent_heat(). Any finite value; negative values are allowed and kept.

lambda

Numeric. Latent heat of vaporization \(\lambda\) [J kg-1], from ef_lambda(). Must lie in [1e6, 1e7] J kg-1 (unit guard, see Details). The same lambda (same method of ef_lambda()) must be used for the cold anchor boundary condition.

Value

A numeric vector of instantaneous evapotranspiration \(ET_{inst}\) [mm h-1] with the common length of the inputs. If the inputs include matrices or arrays (all with the same dim), the result keeps that dim. Negative values (negative le) are returned unchanged.

Details

A depth of water equals the energy per unit area divided by \(\lambda \rho_w\) (FAO-56, chapter 3, box 8). For a flux \(LE\) in W m-2 = J s-1 m-2, the energy accumulated at that rate during one hour is \(3600 LE\), so $$ET_{inst} = \frac{1000 \cdot 3600 \cdot LE}{\lambda \rho_w}$$ where 1000 is mm m-1, 3600 is s h-1, \(\lambda\) is lambda [J kg-1] and \(\rho_w\) = 1000 kg m-3 is the density of water (FAO-56, chapter 3, box 8; internal constant, not an argument). With \(\rho_w\) = 1000 kg m-3 this is numerically \(3600 LE / \lambda\).

The SEBAL Idaho manual writes \(ET_{inst} = 3600\, \lambda ET / \lambda\) in mm h-1 (Waters et al., 2002, p. 34, Eq. 42), i.e. kg m-2 h-1, which is mm h-1 with \(\rho_w\) = 1000 kg m-3: numerically identical to the form above. The notation \(3600 LE / (\lambda \rho_w)\) attributed to METRIC by secondary sources gives m h-1, not mm h-1, with \(\lambda\) in J kg-1; the factor 1000 mm m-1 is written explicitly here.

Unit guard: a lambda given in MJ kg-1 (about 2.45) instead of J kg-1 would silently give an evapotranspiration 1e6 times too large. Values of lambda outside [1e6, 1e7] J kg-1 therefore raise an error of class earthflux_domain_error. The interval is a control of units, not a physical range.

A negative le gives a negative evapotranspiration (condensation or an energy balance in which \(H > R_n - G\)); it is returned unchanged and without a warning, never set to zero. The diagnostic flag EF_ET_NEGATIVE is assembled by the orchestration layer.

Missing values (NA, NaN) in any input propagate to the corresponding output element, without errors or warnings. Arguments must be numeric (double or integer) and have length 1 or a common length; length-1 arguments are recycled, arrays with a dim are not. Infinite values raise an error of class earthflux_domain_error (also earthflux_input_error).

Verification status: VERIFICADA as a unit conversion (FAO-56, chapter 3, box 8 and Eq. 20, plus 3600 s h-1); checked against the FAO-56 equivalences 1 mm d-1 = 2.45 MJ m-2 d-1 (chapter 1, table 1) and 1 W m-2 = 0.035 mm d-1 (chapter 3, table 3); and VERIFICADA (SEBAL-Idaho 2002) (Waters et al., 2002, Eq. 42, see above). Its notation in Allen et al. (2007) has not been verified (desirable, not blocking).

References

Allen, R. G., Pereira, L. S., Raes, D., & Smith, M. (1998). Crop evapotranspiration: Guidelines for computing crop water requirements (FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56). FAO, Rome. ISBN 92-5-104219-5.

Allen, R. G., Tasumi, M., & Trezza, R. (2007). Satellite-based energy balance for mapping evapotranspiration with internalized calibration (METRIC) - Model. Journal of Irrigation and Drainage Engineering, 133(4), 380-394. doi:10.1061/(ASCE)0733-9437(2007)133:4(380)

Waters, R., Allen, R., Bastiaanssen, W., Tasumi, M., & Trezza, R. (2002). SEBAL: Surface Energy Balance Algorithms for Land. Idaho implementation. Advanced training and users manual (Version 1.0). University of Idaho and Idaho Department of Water Resources.

See also

Other latent heat and evapotranspiration functions: ef_et_daily(), ef_etrf(), ef_latent_heat()

Examples

# 490 W m-2 with the FAO-56 constant lambda: 0.72 mm h-1
ef_et_inst(le = 490, lambda = ef_lambda(method = "constant"))
#> [1] 0.72

# Temperature-dependent lambda (air temperature in K)
ef_et_inst(le = 490, lambda = ef_lambda(303.15, method = "fao56"))
#> [1] 0.7258751

# Negative LE is kept: -0.072 mm h-1
ef_et_inst(le = c(490, -49, NA), lambda = 2.45e6)
#> [1]  0.720 -0.072     NA
